title: Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook — Integrations, Escalations, QBRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended processes for enterprise onboarding, third-party integrations, escalation handling, known issues and workarounds, and quarterly business review (QBR) health checks. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers (L2/L3), and partner-facing SREs.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Hosted API (Redwood API), Dedicated, and Private deployments; integrations (API keys, webhooks, private networking); operational readiness for production workloads.
- Audience: CSMs, SEs, Support, SRE, Solutions Architects, and Customer Engineering.

High-level summary:
- A prescriptive onboarding checklist to shorten time-to-first-success for enterprise customers.
- A clear escalation playbook with severity definitions, SLAs, and contact paths.
- Integration guide checklist and example configuration snippets for common patterns (API, VPC, webhooks).
- Centralized known-issues table with reproducible symptoms and workarounds.
- Quarterly health-check and QBR agenda and metrics to track reliability and cost.

Owners and roles:
- Playbook owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success) — primary editor for this doc.
- Escalation owner: Miguel Torres (Support Engineering lead) — maintains on-call matrix and runbooks.
- Integration owner: Priya Desai (Solutions Engineering) — maintains integration templates and sample configs.
- On-call / incident owner: Eng SRE pager duty (policy: CS-P1-Escalation).

Pre-onboarding checklist (to complete before kickoff):
1. Contract & billing validated: Account ID, billing owner, contract start date.
2. Security review: NDA executed, required compliance evidence provided (SOC2/ISO as applicable).
3. Account provisioning: Create account in Redwood Console, generate API key(s) with least privilege.
4. Networking prep: Confirm IP allowlist or VPC peering requirements for Dedicated/Private.
5. Data classification & retention: Confirm customer data residency and retention requirements.

Kickoff agenda (30–60 minutes recommended):
- Introductions and success criteria (CSM + customer execs + SE).
- High-level architecture review (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Integration approach and timeline (API key flow, webhooks, batching).
- SLO & cost targets: latency targets, tokens per second, monthly token budget.
- Next steps and owners.

Onboarding implementation checklist (technical):
- Step 1: API access
  - Create scoped API key (Console > API Keys).
  - Provide example curl and SDK snippet.
  - Validate basic generation and embedding requests.
- Step 2: Authentication & least privilege
  - Configure key rotation cadence (recommended every 90 days).
  - Enable read-only keys for observability if required.
- Step 3: Networking (if Dedicated/Private)
  - Provide VPC peering config or VPN details.
  - Validate routes, NAT, and security group rules.
- Step 4: Webhooks & eventing
  - Register webhook endpoint in Console and validate with test payloads.
  - Configure retries (exponential backoff) and idempotency tokens.
- Step 5: Observability and alerts
  - Ensure customer has access to Console dashboards and traces.
  - Configure alerting thresholds (see Observability thresholds table below).

Observability thresholds (recommended defaults):
| Metric | Warning | Critical | Owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 95th latency (token gen) | 200ms | 500ms | Customer SRE / Redwood SRE |
| Error rate (5m rolling) | 1% | 3% | Support Engineering |
| Queue depth / backpressure | 50 concurrent | 200 concurrent | Eng Platform |
| Token usage burn-rate vs committed | 80% of committed | 100%+ | Customer Success / Finance |

Escalation playbook (severity definitions and steps):
- Severity 1 (P1): Production outage affecting revenue or core user flows, no acceptable workaround. Target response: 15 min, resolution or mitigation 4 hours (SLA internal).
- Severity 2 (P2): Degraded service causing significant customer impact (intermittent failures, higher latency). Target response: 30 min, mitigation 24 hours.
- Severity 3 (P3): Partial loss of non-critical functionality or isolated customer issue. Target response: 4 hours, fix in next patch.
- Severity 4 (P4): Feature request, minor bug, or documentation issue. Target response: 1 business day.

Escalation steps (for Support CSM/SE):
1. Triage in Support queue: collect request ID, account ID, region, model, request payload, and timestamps.
2. Reproduce & classify severity. If P1/P2, immediately open incident in PagerDuty (policy CS-P1-Escalation) and notify CSM + customer.
3. Add SRE and Eng owners to incident bridge.
4. Maintain customer-facing log: issue summary, mitigations, ETA, and next steps (update every 60 minutes for P1).
5. Post-incident: publish postmortem per incident-review guidelines and set remediation owner.

Escalation contacts (primary channels):
- Support portal: support.redwoodinference.com (preferred for ticket tracking)
- Email (for enterprise): support@redwoodinference.com (monitored 24x7)
- Slack: #support-enterprise (for low-latency coordination)
- PagerDuty: CS-P1-Escalation (on-call SRE & Support Engineering)

Integration guide (common patterns and examples):
- API keys & SDKs: Use short-lived keys for automated services when possible, rotate every 90 days. Example curl:
  curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>\" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/text/generate -d '{\"model\":\"rwd/gpt-3.5-inference\",\"input\":\"Hello\"}'
- Webhooks: Configure retries (3 attempts with exponential backoff) and verify signatures (HMAC-SHA256 using webhook secret).
- Batch & caching: For high-throughput use cases, enable batching at the SDK level (recommended batch size 8–32 depending on payload size). Use the Console cache settings to configure prefix caching for conversational workloads.

Sample integration config table:
| Setting | Example | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| API endpoint | https://api.redwoodinference.com | Region-aware endpoints available (us-west-2, eu-west-1) |
| Auth | Bearer API key | Scoped keys for read-only / generate / admin |
| Webhook retry | 3 attempts | Exponential backoff 1m, 2m, 4m |
| VPC peering cidr | 10.1.0.0/16 | Provide at least one route and subnet mapping |

Known issues & workarounds (living table):
- ISSUE-2027-001: Intermittent 500s on long-sequence generation
  - Symptoms: 500 errors after ~8k tokens on rwd/gpt-4-like models.
  - Probable cause: KV cache eviction due to unexpected sequence fragmentation.
  - Workaround: Reduce max_tokens per request to < 7k or switch to the longer-context model variant rwd/gpt-4x-long.
  - Owner: Eng Serving Runtime (triage: Miguel Torres)
- ISSUE-2026-045: Webhook signature mismatch for certain proxies
  - Symptoms: Customer webhook receiver rejects events with invalid signature.
  - Probable cause: Intermediate reverse proxy stripping headers or altering payload (e.g., content-encoding change).
  - Workaround: Instruct customer to validate raw body and configure proxy to preserve headers; enable alternative validation via a nonce header.
  - Owner: Solutions Engineering (Priya Desai)
- ISSUE-2026-089: Elevated token burn during A/B rollout
  - Symptoms: Unexpected spike in token usage after canary rollout to production.
  - Probable cause: Lost caching due to model variant mismatch and small request variations.
  - Workaround: Use deterministic prompt scaffolding and enable prefix caching; rollback canary if cost exceeds threshold.
  - Owner: Customer Success + Redwood Optimize

Support process and SLAs (customer-facing framework):
- Response SLAs (for enterprise support tier):
  - P1: 15-minute acknowledgement, continuous updates until mitigation.
  - P2: 30-minute acknowledgement, updates every 2 hours.
  - P3: 4-hour acknowledgement, updates daily.
  - P4: 1 business-day acknowledgement.
- Resolution target: depends on root cause; follow escalation playbook for timelines and interim mitigations.
- Ticket lifecycle: New -> Triage -> Investigation -> Escalation (if needed) -> Customer Communication -> Resolution -> Postmortem (if P1/P2).

Health checks & QBR materials:
Monthly health-check checklist:
- Service availability (last 30d uptime) >= 99.9% for Dedicated/Hosted customers with SLA.
- 95th percentile latency within target.
- Error rate (5m rolling) < 1% for production traffic.
- Token usage vs committed: within 80% of committed spend.
- Open critical issues: zero P1s open, P2s should have active mitigations.

QBR agenda (recommended):
1. Welcome & attendees (5m)
2. Business goals & success metrics review (10m)
3. Reliability & incidents review (10m)
4. Usage and cost review (10m)
5. Roadmap & upcoming changes (10m)
6. Action items and owners (5m)

QBR metrics table examples to prepare:
| Metric | Window | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Uptime | 30d | >= 99.9% |
| 95th latency | 7d | < 200ms (hosted) |
| Error rate | 7d | < 1% |
| Token usage vs committed | 30d | <= 100% (preferably <= 80%) |
| Cost per 1k tokens | 30d | target agreed in contract |

Postmortem and follow-through:
- For any P1/P2 impacting enterprise customers, perform a blameless postmortem within 72 hours. Include timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action owner with due dates. Track remediation in Eng Platform or Jira and link to the customer-facing incident summary.

Templates and artifact checklist (what to leave the customer):
- Integration playbook customized for customer (markdown + sample configs).
- Console access with scoped API keys and dashboard links.
- Runbook excerpt for customer ops team (incident triggers and mitigations).
- QBR slide pack template populated with metrics and actions.

Appendix — useful links and internal runbooks:

- Integration templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/api-key-rotation
